quote: The rise of large language models (LLMs) has revolutionized dialogue systems, enabling more dynamic and personalized interactions . Among these advancements, role-playing agents (RPAs) have emerged, with agents assigned specific characters or personas.

To evaluate the emotional fidelity of RPAs, we design six metrics ... and conduct extensive experiments on various LLMs with role‑playing methods ... We use the single‑turn and multi‑turn dialogue datasets derived from the script of classic TV show "Friends" (PELD‑single and PELD‑multi).

quote: we design six metrics across three evaluation settings to quantitatively measure how well RPAs maintain emotional fidelity with the characters they portray.

We design six metrics at both the micro and macro levels. At the micro level, we focus on the consistency between the emotions ... We introduce Emotional Consistency Score (EC), its lower bound (EC low), upper bound (EC upp), Relative Emotional Consistency (REC), and Semantic Similarity (SS). At the macro level, we introduce Emotional Distribution Divergence (EDD) and Relative Character Divergence (RCD).
